subject: physics
title: Electric motors and loudspeakers
key_idea: (AQA: Higher tier) A coil carrying a current in a magnetic field has forces on its two sides in opposite directions, so it rotates. This is the basis of an electric motor. (Separate science) A loudspeaker uses the motor effect to turn a changing current into a vibrating cone that makes sound.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) A coil of wire carrying a current in a magnetic field tends to rotate. This is the basis of an electric motor. It uses the motor effect.

items.text: There is a magnetic field between the poles of the magnets. The current in the coil produces a magnetic field around the wire.
The two fields interact, so a force acts on each side of the coil.
The current is in opposite directions in the two sides of the coil. So the forces on the two sides are in opposite directions: one up, one down.
The two forces work together to turn the coil around its axle.

blocks.text: Each force is given by F = B × I × l, so increasing B, I or the length of wire in the field increases the force. Pick a change to the motor.

diagram.alt: Pick a change to an electric motor and see the effect on the force on the coil and how it rotates.

options.label: Increase the current
options.explanation: A bigger current gives a bigger force on the coil.

options.label: Reduce the current
options.explanation: A smaller current gives a smaller force on the coil.

options.label: Use a stronger magnet
options.explanation: A stronger field gives a bigger force.

options.label: Add more turns to the coil
options.explanation: More wire in the field means a bigger force.

options.label: Reverse the current
options.explanation: Reversing the current reverses the force.

options.label: Swap the poles of the magnet
options.explanation: Reversing the field reverses the force.

items: Forces on the two sides of the coil are in opposite directions, so the coil rotates.
A bigger current, a stronger magnet or more turns makes it rotate faster.

blocks.text: (AQA: Higher tier) Loudspeakers and headphones use the motor effect. They turn variations in current into pressure variations in sound waves.

diagram.alt: Put the steps for how a moving-coil loudspeaker produces a sound wave in order.
steps: A current in the coil creates a magnetic field around the coil.
The field interacts with the field of the permanent magnet.
A resultant force acts on the coil, which moves the cone.
When the direction of the current reverses, the direction of the force reverses.
The cone vibrates and produces a sound wave.

items: A changing current makes the coil and cone move back and forth.
This produces pressure variations in the air: a sound wave.

checks.q: Explain why the coil in a simple electric motor rotates when there is a current in it.
checks.a: The current produces a magnetic field that interacts with the field of the magnets. The current is in opposite directions in the two sides of the coil, so the forces on them are in opposite directions. These forces turn the coil.

checks.q: Give two changes that would make the coil of an electric motor rotate faster.
checks.a: Any two from: increase the current, use a stronger magnet, add more turns of wire to the coil.

checks.q: Explain what happens to the force on the cone of a loudspeaker when the direction of the current reverses.
checks.a: The direction of the force reverses, so the cone moves the other way.

blocks.text: A split-ring commutator keeps the coil turning in the same direction.

items: Each half turn, the two halves of the commutator swap from one brush to the other.
This reverses the current in the coil every half turn.
So the current in the left side and in the right side of the coil is always in the same direction relative to the magnet, and the forces keep the coil rotating.

worked_example.question:
A student made a moving-coil loudspeaker.

Explain how a moving-coil loudspeaker produces a sound wave.
answer_points: A current creates a magnetic field around the coil.
This interacts with the permanent magnet field.
This produces a (resultant) force causing the coil or cone to move.
When the direction of the current reverses, the direction of the force reverses, producing a sound wave.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each point. This question is Separate science.

blocks.text: Explaining how the force on a conductor makes a coil rotate in an electric motor is Physics only (Separate science) on this specification.

worked_example.question:
A simple electric motor has a coil of wire between the poles of two magnets.

Explain why the coil rotates when a current passes through it.
answer_points: The current in the coil causes a magnetic field.
The magnetic field of the current-carrying wire interacts with the magnetic field of the magnets and causes a force to act on the wire.
The forces on either side of the coil are opposite: up on one side and down on the other. These two forces work together to cause rotation around the axle.
worked_example.tip: Any two of the points score. Fleming's left-hand rule is ignored.

items: In a motor, energy is transferred from the electrical energy store to the kinetic energy store.
In a motor, the current and magnetic field cause motion.
